 Advertisement Fire at Stanislaus County wildlife center kills approximately 40 animals
 Advertisement Updated: 10:39 PM PST Nov 18, 2026 Editorial Standards ⓘ Nijzel Dotson Digital Producer Fire at Stanislaus County wildlife center kills approximately 40 animals
 Updated: 10:39 PM PST Nov 18, 2026 Editorial Standards ⓘ Nijzel Dotson Digital Producer HUGHSON, Calif. — A fire at the Stanislaus Wildlife Care Center severely damaged the facility and left nearly 40 animals dead. 
 The fire started after staff left around 4 p.m. Valentine Wright, part of the staff, told KCRA 3 the hospital facility is likely completely non functional. While the animals inside the building were killed, 100 caged animals outside of the building survived. 
 Advertisement "This is really devastating for us," Wright said. "We still have a whole lot of animals to take care of, and we're not going to have a lot to take care of them." 
 Fire officials are investigating the cause of the fire.
